name: gaining
description: Delight caused by obtaining something you had previously wanted.
perceptions: Something I had wanted is now mine.
examples: the world seems to have changed for the better

variations.name: winning a game or contest
variations.description: Delight caused by winning a game or contest.
perceptions: I wanted to be on the winning side in that challenge.
That hope or prediction took place.

guidance.description: See the entry about sportsmanship in 'losing'.

variations.name: winning an important contest you were predicted to lose
variations.description: Delight caused by winning a challenge where you or your side were the predicted losers.
perceptions: We should have lost this challenge.
We must have done something right, gotten lucky, or are more skillful than given credit.

guidance.description: See the entry about sportsmanship in 'losing'.

examples: being on the winning side of an election

variations.name: gaining a loved one
variations.description: Delight caused by gaining an important new social connection.
perceptions: A new person has entered into the inner circle of my life.
I'm looking forward to having life experiences with this person or pet.

variations.name: gaining a very important asset
variations.description: Delight caused by acquiring something considered important to survival or to an identity.
perceptions: I've got something new that will help me survive or advance an important social identity.
results: desire to share the news with others

commentaries.quote: Phrases like 'gaining weight' and 'gaining enemies' can be interpreted to mean 'losing fitness' and 'losing friends'.

When you've had a relatively easy life where you have most everything you really want, 'gaining' things seems like the norm. That can make 'not gaining' feel like 'losing', and actual loss feel intolerable.
It's not whether you win or lose, but how you play the game.
Too few rejoice at a friend's good fortune.

names: winning an important contest you were predicted to lose
